messages:
maria: Quick check — onboarding zeta-7b/v1. Pushed manifest to registry (s3://redwood-artifacts/prod/zeta-7b/v1) and the ingest CI is failing with a 403 when requesting presign. Anyone seen this pattern? @registry-service :eyes:

registry-service: automated: presign request denied — origin ACL mismatch. Registry requires either a bucket policy allowing account 123456789012 or objects to be public-read. See log: `presign: denied origin s3://redwood-artifacts/prod/zeta-7b/v1/model.bin (acl=private)`.

sanjay: We hit this before with HF mirror jobs — the HF->S3 uploader sets private ACLs by default. CI presign assumes cross-account read or public. Quick option: re-upload with `--acl public-read` or add a bucket policy.

oliver: For a quick unblock I pointed the ingest to a fallback bucket that has public-read: s3://redwood-fallback/zeta-7b/v1 — presign passes there. But we still need a proper fix so the registry can prefer primary origin and fall back automatically.

maria: Is there a canonical priority field in our manifest schema? Right now we list origins as an array. We need an explicit priority or 'failover_uri' so the runtime can route without manual edit.

sanjay: We actually added an optional `priority` (int) to origin entries in a private branch last quarter but never documented it. PR: https://git.redwood/ingest/+/pr/812 (adds priority and origin_type). Note: presign TTL mismatch too — ingest job issues 2h presigns, registry-service expects 15m short-lived tokens, which led to token reuse errors in tests.

maria: Good catch on TTL. Also saw tokenizer eval failures after the mirror: BLEU/regression spikes. Tokenizer manifest stripped `special_tokens_map` during the HF mirror job. The model loads but eval harness shows BOS/EOS id shifts.

oliver: Tokenizer gotcha: HF "fast" tokenizers will serialize slightly different fields depending on how they were trained (legacy BPE vs. new training). Our loader currently errors if `merges.txt` is absent and falls back to the slow python path which loses `padding_side` and `cls_token`. Suggest adding a tokenizer_sanity step in preflight that asserts presence of: tokenizer.json, vocab, merges/merges.txt or tokenizer.model, and non-empty special_tokens_map.

sanjay: I'll add a lint stage in the ingest CI to check: 1) object ACL (public-read or bucket policy), 2) x-amz-meta-origin header exists, 3) `tokenizer.json` or `tokenizer.model` present, and 4) tokens for `<bos>`, `<eos>` in special_tokens_map. Draft patch here: https://git.redwood/ingest/+/pr/813 — runs lightweight checks locally via `python -m ingest.lint manifest.json`.

ci-bot: pipeline update: ingest-manifest-lint job added to the `on-upload` workflow — https://ci.redwood/pipelines/ingest/1234 (runs on PRs).

maria: Two asks from product side: (1) can registry-service accept presign requests for private objects if caller supplies an account role (we use cross-account assume-role in Dedicated flows)? (2) Can we add docs for manifest `priority` and a `failover_uri` field so partner uploads know expectations.

registry-service: We can support role-aware presign if the caller passes an `x-allow-role-presign` header and we validate STS caller ARN against allowed roles. I'll open a PR to add an opt-in flag and a compatibility mode for current ingesters.

oliver: Proposed action items: assign @sanjay to land the ingest-lint CI, @registry-service to add role-aware presign header and TTL alignment, and @maria to update onboarding docs with `priority`/`failover_uri` and tokenizer preflight requirements. I'll add a checklist item to the model onboarding board. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — once PRs are in I'll re-run the zeta-7b ingest. If anyone wants to sanity-check the tokenizer patch locally:

```bash
# local tokenizer sanity check
python -c "from ingest.tools import tokenizer_sanity; print(tokenizer_sanity('s3://redwood-artifacts/prod/zeta-7b/v1'))"
```

sanjay: I'll start on the CI change this afternoon, ping here when you re-run so I can watch logs.

oliver: Noted — adding this to the onboarding retro. Thanks folks.
